title: Terminal tinkering after dinner
story: Most weeknights end with tea, a terminal window, and one problem small enough to finish before I start bargaining with myself about sleep. The rule is simple: one script, one fix, one clean rerun. If it turns into a grand plan, I save it for another night.
takeaway: A hobby survives when the scope still fits the hour.

title: Chasing a tone at midnight
story: Some nights the first movement of the Moonlight Sonata drifts in and everything slows down — the room goes quiet, the triplets keep rolling, and I forget I was doing anything else. Beethoven wrote it in a season of heartbreak, and you can hear it: each note lands like something he couldn't quite say out loud.
takeaway: The best music doesn't demand your attention — it just makes everything else disappear.

title: Weekly learning notes
story: Last weekend's note: idempotency keys, from a Stripe engineering post on retries at the API boundary. The practical example was this site's contact form — a Worker endpoint that could be retried from a flaky connection, where a stored key stops a double-submit. The open question is still what happens when the client retries faster than the key's TTL, and it's the line I keep rereading. The concept I can look up. The question is the part that's mine.
takeaway: Questions stay alive when I write them down.

title: Micro-interaction motion lab
story: Spent a weekend on the Quick Look card's hover transition on this site's work detail pages, nudging duration between 120ms and 240ms. 180ms won. The version I was proudest of — a spring with a small overshoot — was the first one I cut. It called attention to itself, which meant it was doing the card's job and its own.
takeaway: Good motion disappears into the gesture it serves.

title: Sample/patch of the week
story: This week it's the Soft Piano patch from Spitfire Audio LABS. I auditioned a dozen others in Ableton and kept coming back to this one because the felt hammers mute the top octave just enough — the way it sits under a slow triplet figure without asking for attention. Everything else got deleted before Sunday.
takeaway: The shortlist gets sharper every time I throw something off it.

title: Typography rabbit hole
story: Started with Matthew Butterick's Practical Typography on a Saturday morning and ended up pasting the same paragraph into Figma at every line length between 45 and 75 characters. Somewhere around 65ch on a 16-pixel base versus 55ch on 18, I could finally feel the difference instead of just seeing it. Now I check rhythm, spacing, contrast, and scan paths before I trust a clean-looking screen.
takeaway: A readable page is tuned by ear, the way a mix is.

title: Favorite tool of the month
story: Lazygit earned the spot the second week of April, somewhere around the third time I reached for it without thinking. The first ten minutes of a coding session used to go to interactive staging — cycling through git add -p, losing my place when I hit escape by accident. Now they don't. That's the whole test. A month of quiet wins, no ceremony.
takeaway: Trust is what's left after a tool stops surprising me.

title: One-take loop nights
story: I want a standing 30-minute session where I build one loop in a single take, leave the mistakes in, and practice recovering instead of restarting.

title: Build a playful terminal toy
story: I built a tiny scripted terminal interaction around a letter from my dad and spent far too long tuning the pauses so it felt discovered instead of dumped on the screen. It is a small toy, but it reminded me that interface timing can carry emotion.
takeaway: Pacing can make interface copy hit like narrative.

title: One-page field guide
story: I want to keep a single page of repeat lessons from side experiments: what surprised me, what broke first, and which fix I would try sooner next time.
takeaway: Write the lesson down before the cleanup hides it.
